correctness.rationale: For iid draws on m>=2 strictly positive categories, the first t-1 distinct labels in {C=i,T=t} comprise i plus t-2 others, giving K_{i,t}=(t-1)! p_i^2 e_{t-2}(p_{-i}) on the exact support 2<=t<=m+1. For p_i=p>p_j=q and E_k=e_k(p_{-{i,j}}), adjacent ratios K_{i,k+2}/K_{j,k+2} decrease because the cross-product difference (p-q)(E_k^2-E_{k-1}E_{k+1}) is positive, by strict Newton log-concavity and E_{-1}=E_{m-1}=0. The empty remaining-vector m=2 case gives the same strict endpoint comparison. Positive denominators cover the final time, and transitivity gives all t<u minors. Row normalization preserves likelihood-ratio ordering, implying strict conditional CDF and mean ordering. The direct identity K_{i,t}-K_{j,t}=(t-1)!(p-q)[(p+q)E_k+pq E_{k-1}]>0 covers both endpoint indices; uniform p gives independence by symmetry, and nonconstant p violates independence by strict odds variation. I independently checked 346 rational probability vectors with m=2..6, including 82 exhaustive first-repeat sequence enumerations at m<=4, and separately reconstructed the 7-entry Git tree SHA. These finite checks corroborate rather than prove the all-real theorem.
residual_risks: Finite enumeration is not a universal proof; strict Newton inequality and positive support establish universality.
No claims for zero-probability categories, dependent draws or later repeat events are assessed.
The source script was read as evidence; the reported independent computations did not rely on its PASS string.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Set i=low and j=high in the 2026-10-18 statement: K_low,u/K_high,u > K_low,t/K_high,t. Cross multiply to get K_high,t K_low,u > K_high,u K_low,t, the November 8 theorem exactly. Normalize K rows to obtain T|C; standard one-crossing yields all CDF/mean inequalities. From the same earlier K formula, K_high,t-K_low,t=(t-1)!(p-q)[(p+q)E_k+pq E_{k-1}]>0; strict odds excludes C,T independence for unequal p and uniform symmetry gives independence. Thus there is no surviving new theorem after prior implications are taken.

originality.rationale: A 2026-10-18 published Resultary theorem already asserts the identical all-m, all-positive-p, all-times marked joint mass K_{i,t}=(t-1)!p_i^2 e_{t-2}(p_{-i}) and for p_i<p_j strictly INCREASING posterior odds P(C=i|T=t)/P(C=j|T=t) as t increases. Multiplying by the positive time normalization and swapping i,j gives EXACTLY the November 8 strict reverse likelihood-ratio minor K_{j,t}K_{i,u}>K_{j,u}K_{i,t} for t<u. Consequently the time-given-mark strict likelihood-ratio order is a Bayes/2x2-minor reformulation, not a new result. The CDF and mean consequences follow from standard strict likelihood-ratio order; nonindependence for unequal p follows from the previously proved strict posterior odds, while full uniformity gives independence by symmetry. The joint mass row comparison follows by a one-line subtraction from the same published K formula. Therefore the candidate entire theorem is a restatement plus immediate consequences of an earlier full-text publication; this is decisive theorem-level prior coverage, not mere title similarity.
residual_risks: Historical search cannot exclude all other predecessors, but direct published 2026-10-18 coverage suffices to reject this November 8 claim regardless.
Additional early Holst/Flajolet sources were not freshly read in full; their contents are not needed for the decisive prior-implication comparison.
The November 8 package self-review did not mention the decisive October 18 theorem and its different conditional orientation.

value.rationale: The conditional repeated-label/time likelihood-ratio property is a natural and potentially useful invariant of heterogeneous occupancy sampling; the strict stochastic-order and independence conclusions are substantive interpretations. But here they are algebraic reorientations or immediate standard consequences of the October 18 complete theorem for precisely the same K_{i,t} table. The extra row-dominance identity is a one-line difference of an already published probability formula, with no new motivated boundary, parameter or classification. Independent exact-rational verification, a more detailed presentation and the practical relevance do not establish an independently valuable new mathematical contribution after full prior implication is accounted for.
residual_risks: The mathematical property remains useful as a corollary of the earlier result, though it should not be accepted as a separate original finding.
No generalization to dependent sampling, second repeat, or previously unknown parameter range survives in the candidate.

limitations: No source or public file changed; all historical ledger rows preserved.
Finite checks corroborate only bounded rational instances, not universal real-valued proof.
